guias.subtitulo: How to use and level up this system
guias.resumo: The Collection, also called Album or Emaki on the screens, turns the warriors you own into bonuses for all your warriors in battle. Activating and upgrading cards costs no gold, Dragon Stones or materials: each card's limit follows the real stars of the matching warrior.

visao.x: Go to Support on the home screen and choose Collection. The system opens for regular accounts at level 12; the card may appear earlier and stay locked until you meet the requirement.

The next sections explain how it works, how it levels up and where to get materials. The cost of an upgrade depends on the level and the item you choose. Check the preview of your action before confirming.

blocos.x: Open Support and enter Collection. Access to the Album is unlocked at account level 12. The system card may appear before that, but opening it depends on that level. The level that counts is the account's; you do not need to raise a specific warrior to level 12 to open the system.

Every warrior in the catalog has their own card. Before activation, it stays dimmed and adds no attributes. Once activated, its bonus line enters the Album total. You do not need to put the card's owner in the lineup to benefit from the contribution: the total bonus is applied to the warriors in battle.

The system separates ownership gains from collection gains. Getting a warrior or promoting their stars creates the chance to update the card; you must confirm Activate, Upgrade or Upgrade All to register the Album's new star. Visiting the screen or looking at a preview does not make this update.

secoes.titulo: How to find and activate a card

blocos.x: The list is split into the ATK, DEF and SKL tabs. They match the warrior's class, not the attribute the card grants: a card in the ATK tab can also add DEF and HP to the collection total. Pick a tab and browse the cards; the list is horizontal and shows arrows when there are more cards than visible space.

Cards that can be updated come before the others. Then come the ones already activated, sorted by stars, aptitude and name. The red dots help you find an available upgrade in the tab, on the card or past an arrow. They are neither a random reward nor a material you have to buy.

items: Choose a warrior you already own. A card for a warrior you do not have warns that you need to own them.
Tap Activate to open the comparison between the current card and the result allowed by the warrior's stars.
Check the before and after and confirm Activate. For a card that is already active, the same process uses the Upgrade button.
Go back to the list and check the registered stars. A card that has reached the warrior's current star only gets an upgrade again when that warrior gains more stars.

blocos.x: The single confirmation takes the card straight up to the warrior's current star. It is not a purchase of one star per tap. If the card is at 1★ and the warrior already has 5★, one confirmation registers 5★ in the Album. The system does not consume copies, fragments or units of the warrior to make this update.

Upgrade All works only on the selected tab. The game asks for confirmation and updates every eligible card of that class up to the current star of its owner. To update ATK, DEF and SKL, visit all three tabs. If no card in the tab can go up, a notice appears and nothing changes.

The cost of promoting the warrior belongs to the Warrior screen. The Collection does not remove that earlier cost, but it also does not charge again for copying stars you have already earned. A card cannot be advanced beyond the real warrior to get bonuses early.

The Attributes panel shows ATK, HP, DEF and the ATK, DEF and HP rates added up from all activated cards. The first three are fixed values; the rates are percentages. The panel's order may be ATK, HP, DEF, while this guide's table uses ATK, DEF, HP to make comparison easier.

The warrior's aptitude and the card's star decide the bonus line. The lines already represent that card's total in its current state: when you reach 5★, replace its old contribution with the 5★ line. Do not add the 1★, 2★, 3★, 4★ and 5★ lines as if they were five cards.

In the table below, the last column applies separately to each of the three rates. For example, 1.5% means +1.5% ATK, +1.5% DEF and +1.5% HP, not a single percentage split among those attributes. The values are transcribed from the Album table.

Goku uses aptitude 12 in the catalog consulted. A card of that aptitude at 1★ contributes +40 ATK, +15 DEF and +320 HP, with no rates. If it can be updated to 3★, it contributes +80 ATK, +30 DEF and +640 HP. The gain from that update is +40 ATK, +15 DEF and +320 HP; the confirmation costs no resources.

At aptitude 12, going from 3★ to 5★ keeps the fixed values at +80 ATK, +30 DEF and +640 HP, but adds 0.4% to each rate. An update can improve only the percentages. Do not conclude there was no benefit just because the fixed numbers did not change.

Adding an aptitude 12 card at 5★ and an aptitude 13 card at 3★, the combined contribution is +200 ATK, +70 DEF, +1,600 HP and +1.3% to each rate. This sum counts only those two cards; your account's total panel may be larger because it includes other cards already activated.

There is no exclusive material for activating the cards: the condition is owning the matching warrior. After that, upgrade opportunities come from the stars they really have. The Album does not recruit warriors, deliver copies or promote stars; those actions belong to their own systems.

The bonus catalog consulted contains 55 lines: aptitudes 12, 13 and 14 have lines from 1★ to 15★; aptitude 15 has lines from 1★ to 10★. That describes the table's coverage; it does not prove that every warrior and every promotion is reachable in the current version. A card's availability still depends on the catalog and real ownership.

There are no bonus lines for aptitudes 11 or 16 in that table, nor for aptitude 15 above 10★. The current rule returns zero bonus when a line is missing. For that reason, this guide does not project attributes for LR or for stars that are not in the data. Check the game's Attributes panel instead of extrapolating the progression of another aptitude.

The app's individual preview shows up to three changed attributes; the total panel shows six. A bonus can exist even when it does not appear among the preview's three lines.

guias.subtitulo: How to use and level up this system
guias.resumo: Talent lets you invest Talent Points and gold in trees that improve the lineup, classes and combat attributes. Each purchase raises one node by one level; the choices depend on the branches' requirements and can be reset with Dragon Stones.

visao.x: Go to Support on the home screen and choose Talent. The system opens for regular accounts at level 28; the card may appear earlier and stay locked until you meet the requirement.

The next sections explain how it works, how it levels up and where to get materials. The cost of an upgrade depends on the level and the item you choose. Check the preview of your action before confirming.

blocos.x: Open Support and tap Talent. Entering the system requires account level 28. Inside it, each tree has extra requirements: account level and an amount of Talent Points already invested in the tree immediately before it. Having points available in your wallet does not replace invested points.

The first tree has an internal limit of 25, but the normal path through the hub only opens the system at level 28. The second asks for level 50 and 150 points spent in the first; the third, level 70 and 280 spent in the second; the fourth, level 80 and 520 spent in the third. The sum is made from the costs actually paid at each level of each node, not from counting icons or levels.

The catalog contains 48 talents, all with a maximum of 10 levels. The first three trees have 27 nodes in total. The PvP tree contains 21 nodes tied to specific modes; check how those bonuses are limited before investing in it.

Select the tree and tap the talent's icon. The window compares the current level with the next and shows effects and the cost in Talent Points and gold. A locked talent may depend on the account level as well as on another node at level 7. Unlocking the whole tree does not automatically unlock all of its nodes.

The Upgrade action buys exactly one level. The next cost is checked again after the purchase. There is no Upgrade All and no partial spending in this action. If you lack Talent Points or gold, the app opens the resource's Sources; a blocked attempt does not let you gain the level without paying.

The red dot on a tree means at least one talent in it has the requirements and resources to go up. The highlight on a node only shows what you selected. Check the requirements and cost of the chosen node, since nodes in the same tree can have different Talent Point costs.

items: Open the tree available to your account.
Tap the node and read the effect at the current and next level.
Check the account level and the previous node's prerequisite.
Have the required Talent Points and gold; confirm Upgrade.
Repeat only up to the level you want or up to the maximum of 10.

blocos.x: The seven talents in this tree split their effects between the rows. Front corresponds to slots 1-3; back, to slots 4-6. The first node grants HP only to the front and ATK only to the back row. Changing a warrior's position can change which benefit they get.

The next specialization offers fixed values. Then come HP or ATK rates and, finally, damage reduction or increase. The next branch requires level 7 on the node before it: you do not need to max that node at 10 to open the path. The account level limits still apply.

Every node in this tree uses the same cost sequence: 36 Talent Points and 415,000 gold to go from 0 to 10. These are totals for one node; all seven complete add up to 252 points and 2,905,000 gold. The requirement of 150 to open the next tree is investment accumulated across the whole tree.

blocos.x: Attack and Defense Specialist uses the costs below. At level 1, the bonus is HP+80 for the front and ATK+10 for the back; at level 7, HP+560 and ATK+70; at level 10, HP+800 and ATK+100. The factors of these effects grow linearly per level.

Reaching level 7 costs 20 points and 175,000 gold accumulated. This unlocks the two following branches of that node, as long as the tree and the account level are already unlocked. Going from level 7 to 10 costs another 16 points and 240,000 gold. The investment up to 7 also counts toward the 150 points of the next tree.

The root raises HP and ATK of all warriors. The three branches separate ATK, SKL and DEF; then they modify the relationship between classes: ATK against SKL, SKL against DEF and DEF against ATK. The advantage nodes describe a reduction of damage taken and an increase of damage dealt in that specific relationship, not a universal increase in attributes. Each complete node costs 670,000 gold; the points vary according to the stretch of the branch.

secoes.titulo: PvP Tree: catalog and current limitation

blocos.x: The PvP tree has seven themed lines, each with three nodes. In general, I adds ATK and HP; II deals with damage rate and damage reduction; III deals with Supreme damage and defense. Advancing requires level 7 on the previous node. The first line starts at Arena I; the following lines also require node III of the previous line at level 7.

In the implementation consulted, the bonuses for specific areas of this tree are excluded from the function that delivers general Talent passives to the fight and from the attribute projection for CP. Access to the tree does not prove that its specific PvP bonuses are applied in combat. This guide presents its catalog, but does not recommend the spending as a confirmed gain in the modes listed.

There is an old unlock record that cites level 999, but the tabs on this screen use the tree's own requirements: 80 and 520 points. The 48 nodes have no Dragon Stone charge to buy levels in the current data; the Stone cost confirmed here is that of the reset.

secoes.titulo: Resetting a tree or all talents

blocos.x: On the tree with investment, tap Reset. The window shows 500 Dragon Stones and the Talent Points that will be returned. Without ticking the option for the other talents, the action resets only the selected tree. Ticking the option includes all invested trees, with a single charge of 500 Stones.

The reset returns all the Talent Points invested in the selected nodes and 50% of the gold spent on them, rounded down. The levels of those nodes go back to zero. The other half of the gold is not recovered. The requirements of the trees and nodes are recalculated; resetting an earlier tree may leave the next one without the investment required to continue its upgrades.

Example: if the only invested node is Attack and Defense Specialist at level 10, the reset costs 500 Stones and returns 36 Talent Points and 207,500 gold. At level 7, it returns 20 points and 87,500 gold. The reset cost is not deducted from the gold returned; they are different resources.

The reset does not automatically redistribute to another branch. After receiving the refund, buy the desired nodes again and pay their costs. Having points available does not on its own remove the required levels and prerequisites.

Talent Points are the resource specific to talent levels; gold is the second cost. When one of them is missing, the Source window shows the registered paths. For Talent Points, the registered shortcuts include Story, Arena, Elite, Nightmare and Hero Dungeon. These shortcuts do not state an amount of points per victory nor prove a chance of getting points on each attempt.

The acquisition texts provided contain cross-translations with other resources. Do not use sentences about Emblem EXP or Tome as a rule for getting Talent Points. Check the rewards shown in the destination mode. A daily Talent Points task is mentioned in a rule comment, but was not found as a grant in the current catalog consulted; the guide does not promise a fixed daily prize.

General Talent attributes count toward CP according to the target and the real slot in the lineup. Combat effects, relationships between classes and specific areas cannot be indiscriminately converted into a CP number. An upgrade does not guarantee an increase animation: it depends on the team's real CP going up.

Some old level notices differ from the requirement used by the rule: the first node 111, for example, opens at 25, although its condition text cites 30. Normal access to the system remains 28. Use the access requirements and lock states of the current flow, without treating a divergent sentence as a new cost or a new unlock.

items: Normal access through Support requires level 28, although the first tree and its initial node have an internal requirement of 25. Some old notices cite level 30; they differ from the current rule.

The PvP tree opens at level 80 with 520 points invested in the Class tree. Its access does not confirm that the specific bonuses are applied: the implementation consulted excludes them from the general fight passives and from the attribute calculation for CP.

All 48 talents have a maximum of 10 levels and do not charge Stones to buy levels. The point totals of the complete nodes are 252, 450, 652 and 1,359 across the four trees. These totals are not the minimum spending to unlock the next tree.

The shortcuts in the Source window do not prove a chance or an amount of Talent Points. The daily task mentioned in a rule comment was not found as a grant in the catalog consulted; this guide does not promise a fixed daily prize.

guias.subtitulo: How to use and level up this system
guias.resumo: Affinity develops each warrior with the gifts they accept. Levels add their own attributes and Priority; when a stage is completed, Affinity Boost opens the next one. Gifts are consumed, and their EXP must be managed so as not to waste the excess at the stage cap.

visao.x: Go to Support on the home screen and choose Affinity. The system opens for regular accounts at level 36; the card may appear earlier and stay locked until you meet the requirement.

The next sections explain how it works, how it levels up and where to get materials. The cost of an upgrade depends on the level and the item you choose. Check the preview of your action before confirming.

blocos.x: Open Support and enter Affinity. The feature starts to appear at account level 30 and opens at level 36. The catalog consulted lists 80 warriors in 41 gift groups. The player's list shows the warriors from those groups that they really own; a warrior you do not own cannot receive gifts as if they already belonged to the account.

On the left, choose the warrior. The nature filters help find them. On the right, check the stage, the Affinity level and the EXP bar. The level shown on this screen is the Affinity level; it does not directly change the warrior's normal level.

Each group has three accepted gifts. Sharing a group means being able to use the same types of gift, not sharing progression: giving a gift to Goku improves Goku's state. It does not automatically improve Goku SS 3 or Xeno Goku, even if they accept the same foods.

The three gifts appear with name, quantity owned and matching EXP value. One tap consumes one unit and applies its EXP to the chosen warrior. Holding the button repeats single-unit deliveries; repetition ends when you release, leave the button, reach the limit or run out of items.

Delivery does not charge gold or Dragon Stones beyond the gift consumed. It is applied directly; there is no preview that lets you receive the EXP and then cancel the consumption. When the gift runs out, the game may warn about the shortage. If you are already out of the item, the action opens the Source window.
The three gift tiers give 5, 20 or 60 EXP. Acceptance depends on the warrior's family; another food with the same EXP value is not automatically valid for them. Use the three items your screen shows.

In the examples table, the names indicate warriors found in the current catalog; other members of the same group may exist in the data. Check the gifts shown for the chosen warrior, without assuming these table names are exclusive.

secoes.titulo: Seven stages, with their own limits

blocos.x: The implemented progression has stages D, C, B, A, S, SS and SSS. The Affinity level restarts at 0 when moving to a new stage. This does not mean losing the attributes already developed: the first line of the new stage preserves the continuity of the attributes and may raise Priority.

Fill the bar up to the stage's maximum level. Then tap Affinity Boost. This transition does not charge a gift, gold or Stones; it requires that the current stage has reached its maximum and that there is still a next stage. You must perform this Boost to keep feeding the warrior.

The table shows the exact EXP from level 0 up to each stage's cap. The five warrior categories use the same EXP cost sequence, although their attributes differ. The accumulated column adds up the completed stages; it is not the EXP shown on the current level's bar.

If a gift completes a level and leftover EXP remains, the rest goes to the next level of the same stage. One gift can raise several levels when there is enough EXP. When it reaches the stage cap, however, the leftover is zeroed. It is not saved for the next stage.

Example: 5 EXP are missing to finish stage D. A gift worth 60 completes that stage, but 55 EXP are discarded. An accepted gift worth 5 solves the same limit with no loss. Near the cap, prefer the smaller units available and release the button as soon as MAX appears.

From the start of stage D up to level 20, 700 EXP are needed. You can complete it exactly with 35 gifts of 20; with 140 gifts of 5; or with 11 gifts of 60 and 2 of 20. These examples use only items accepted by the warrior. There is no combo bonus for alternating food types.

From entering D up to the SSS cap, the progression adds up to 78,300 EXP. Since leftovers do not carry across stages, plan each step separately. Dividing the total by 60 and rounding does not automatically yield an amount that is enough with no loss for all seven limits.

Affinity raises the chosen warrior's ATK, DEF and HP, plus two attributes defined by their category. ATK warriors get Crit and Anti-Crit; DEF gets Block and Break; SKL, Light and Darkness get damage rate and damage reduction. The percentage value in the table corresponds to each of the two attributes in the pair.

The bonus is specific to the warrior. A reserve warrior's Affinity does not deliver their ATK, DEF or HP values to another character in the lineup. Priority plays a different role: it goes into the account's Team Speed, together with the quality contributions of the warriors owned.

In the current data, groups have no extra speedup for completing all of their warriors. Therefore, the guide does not promise a speed prize for closing out a gift family. The contributions from Achievements and Biography cited by rules in the original are also not implemented in this calculation.
The final table shows the total Affinity at stage SSS, level 100, not the increase from a single gift. The same total requires 78,300 EXP of progression for any category; the attribute values vary.

Goku is in the ATK category in the catalog consulted and accepts Rice Balls, Cherry Lobster and Grilled Steak, with 5/20/60 EXP. At the start, D 0, his Affinity does not add attributes yet. A gift of 20 fills the first requirement and takes him to D 1: +24 ATK and Priority 1.
At D 10, Goku's bonuses are +48 ATK, +16 DEF, +160 HP, +0.2% Crit, +0.2% Anti-Crit and Priority 10. At D 20, they are +96 ATK, +32 DEF, +320 HP, +0.4% on each of those rates and Priority 20.

When using Boost from D 20 to C 0, the same +96 ATK, +32 DEF, +320 HP and 0.4% rates are preserved; Priority goes from 20 to 30. The first EXP requirement of the new stage is 30. You can keep gifting after closing the Boost window.

For ATK, DEF and SKL categories, each entry into stages C through SSS delivers 2,000 gold and 5 Dragon Stones; there is another equal prize on reaching SSS 100. That is seven grants in total along this path, adding up to 14,000 gold and 35 Stones. The current prize records do not include Light or Darkness: do not project the same reward for those categories.

secoes.titulo: Gift sources and care with names

blocos.x: The Source window is the game's own path when a food is missing. For the Goku group's gifts, the catalog points to Daily Trial, Serpent Road, Bond Shop and, depending on the item, Grocery, Arena Shop, Trial Shop, Weekly Pack and Cross-Server Arena. The list varies by gift; do not treat all these routes as sources of every food.

These records provide shortcuts, but not quantities, current stock or verified chances. Some acquisition texts are crossed in translation. Use the item's name and the rewards actually shown at the destination before buying or spending an attempt. An advertised source does not mean the item will always be on sale.

This guide's families table uses the names present in the current data. In some items, the name field contains a description sentence instead of a food name; those records were not used in the main examples. The item's identifier can help recognize a gift when there is a translation mismatch.

The Affinity screen has no button to reset the warrior for free. The refund rule belongs to the Rebirth flow. Its calculation gathers the EXP actually invested in the levels and the leftover stored at the current level; it converts that value into the accepted gifts, starting with those of 60 EXP, then 20 and 5.

The refund does not necessarily reproduce the same combination of foods you spent. For example, 700 EXP represent 11 gifts of 60 and 2 of 20 in the refund calculation. EXP already discarded on reaching the cap does not count in the total invested and cannot reappear in this conversion.

The operational limit consulted is stage 7/SSS, level 100. Although old prize records exist for stages 8 and 9, the current rule does not allow reaching them. This guide does not use those records to announce new stages, level 120 or future rewards.

items: Each stage's EXP is the same across the five categories: 700, 2,600, 5,700, 10,800, 17,500, 19,500 and 21,500, adding up to 78,300. The final attributes, however, vary by category.
The families table shows names found in the catalog. Some groups have additional members without an identified name; the examples are not exclusive lists of the warriors who accept each gift.
Light and Darkness have Affinity attributes, but no stage prizes configured. The current limit is SSS, level 100; prize records for later stages do not unlock that progression.

The refund cited under Rebirth explains the conversion of invested EXP into gifts. The costs and requirements of the full action belong to another flow; the Affinity screen does not offer a free reset.

The current groups do not grant additional speed for completing all their members. The Priority developed counts toward Team Speed; the other Affinity attributes belong to the warrior who received the gifts.

guias.resumo: Supreme Stones strengthen the warrior who equips them and, when a complete page meets the conditions, unlock a Supreme effect specific to that warrior. The system opens at account level 42; the other pages arrive at levels 48 and 52.

visao.x: Go to Support on the home screen and choose Supreme - Supreme Stones. The system opens for regular accounts at level 42; the card may appear earlier and stay locked until you meet the requirement.

The next sections explain how it works, how it levels up and where to get materials. The cost of an upgrade depends on the level and the item you choose. Check the preview of your action before confirming.

secoes.titulo: Getting started: warrior, page and sequence

blocos.x: Go to Support > Supreme, choose an owned warrior and open one of the three pages. Each slot asks for a specific order of stone. The order's name identifies the piece that fits that slot; having a stone of another order does not make up for the missing one. The attributes of the equipped stones add to the chosen warrior, even before the page's skill becomes active.

Select the slot and choose a compatible free stone from the Supreme bag. Auto-equip fills the slots for which free stones exist; Remove returns the stones to this system's bag. A single stone unit is not equipped in two places: when you move it, it leaves its previous owner. There is no Gold cost for these swaps.

The page's quality is determined by the worst stone among all of its slots. A Mythic stone next to an Elite one does not turn the page Mythic. If any stone is missing, the skill stays inactive. For the immediate attributes, evaluate the individual stone; to unlock the skill, prioritize completing the sequence and upgrading the piece that limits the page.
Pages and unlocking
The twelve orders
They are slots in the sequence, not twelve character-exclusive pieces of equipment.

A new stone starts at level 0 with no advancements. Upgrading consumes Supreme Essence and raises one level; the quick upgrade repeats that step while there is Essence, stopping at level 10 of the current cycle. It does not advance automatically. At level 10, Advance charges Gold, increases the number of advancements and returns the local level to 0.

That return to 0 does not erase the growth. The accumulated Supreme level is the current level plus ten per advancement. Each advancement also adds an extra step of attribute growth. So a stone with one advancement and level 0 is slightly better than the same stone with no advancement at level 10.

All 72 current stones allow ten advancements. The cap is ten advancements and level 10, equivalent to 110 accumulated upgrades. The rule provides for Evolve when there is a target configuration, but no stone in this catalog has that target: do not plan a rarity transformation through the Evolve button. Better quality depends on getting another stone.
Qualities: example of the Collect order at level 0
Essence cost per level
Multiply by the quality factor: Common 1, Rare 2, Elite 3, Epic 4, Legendary 5 or Mythic 6. The cost is constant across the ten levels of each cycle.
Essence to reach each milestone

Total Supreme Essence that a new stone spends up to each Supreme level milestone (level + 10 per advancement). In parentheses, the spending for that 10-level cycle only. Advancements also charge Gold, which is not included in the count.

blocos.sub: Common, Rare, Elite, Epic, Legendary and Mythic (accumulated total)

blocos.x: From zero to Lv. 110: Epic 10,840, Legendary 13,550 and Mythic 16,260 Essence per stone. For a whole page, multiply by the number of stones.

secoes.titulo: Full example: Epic Collect and Goku

blocos.x: Epic Collect starts with ATK 240, DEF 120 and HP 1920. Ten upgrades cost 160 Supreme Essence and take the attributes to 280 / 140 / 2240. The first advancement costs 40,000 Gold; at level 0 of the new cycle, the stone goes to 284 / 142 / 2272. The next level costs 24 Essence. These values show why level 0 after Advance does not mean going back to the initial strength.

On Goku's first page, the sequence is Power > Punch > Collect. The account needs level 42 to open the slots, but the skill still requires all stones to be Epic or better, a total Supreme level of 60 and Goku with at least four stars. Three Epics at level 10, with no advancement, add up to only 30: enough quality does not replace the growth requirement.

One way to reach 60 is to leave each of the three stones with one advancement and level 10: 20+20+20. Starting from new Epic stones, this example consumes 1,200 Essence and 120,000 Gold in total. Goku's Epic page describes +5% to his own ATK; with all Legendary stones, the described effect is 10%; with all Mythic, 15%. The conditions and the skill change per warrior, so do not copy Goku's sequence to another sheet.

secoes.titulo: Getting stones, Essence and recovering investment

blocos.x: Summon > Supreme offers Gold cards and Dragon Stone cards. Each card's single pull has one free daily chance in the current catalog; the reset uses 05:00. After the free one, the purchase uses the appropriate scroll if there is enough quantity; without it, it charges the indicated currency. The limits are separate per button and count paid purchases, not the number of stones received.

Supreme Essence has one proven direct source: Dismantle free stones. Equipped stones must be removed first. The refund adds the stone's base value and 100% of the Essence used on its levels; it returns 80% of the Gold spent on advancements. For example, dismantling an Epic Collect at level 10 with no advancement returns 520 Essence: 360 from the stone plus 160 invested. With one advancement and level 0, the same example returns 520 Essence and 32,000 Gold.

guias.resumo: Treasure is the permanent Combat Equipment system found in Support. It appears at Lv.40 and opens at account Lv.45. You activate objects with their fragments, raise stars and do Rupture to improve their level. Bonuses accumulate for the team: you do not need to equip a Treasure in a warrior's slot.

visao.x: Go to Support on the home screen and choose Treasure: the team's Combat Equipment. The system opens for regular accounts at level 45; the card may appear earlier and stay locked until you meet the requirement.

The next sections explain how it works, how it levels up and where to get materials. The cost of an upgrade depends on the level and the item you choose. Check the preview of your action before confirming.

secoes.titulo: What a Treasure is and what it is not

blocos.x: This mode has ninety Treasures organized into twenty-five sets. It is separate from the Treasure Hunt Journey in events and from the Bag's chests. Opening a chest with a prize or taking part in a journey does not automatically activate an object from this catalog; for that, gather the specific fragments and confirm the first star.

The catalog has twenty R pieces, twenty-five SR and forty-five SSR. R reach ten stars and have only Lv.1. SR reach ten stars and Lv.13. SSR reach six stars and Lv.13. So a lower star cap is not an error: the SSR family uses a different track.

In the list, compare the name, the attributes, the set and the fragment stock. Each object has its own fragment, which cannot be replaced by another Treasure's fragment. An inactive piece grants no attribute and does not complete the set, even if you already own part of the fragments.

The first star is the activation. It requires twenty fragments for R, thirty for SR and forty for SSR. On confirming, the object enters Lv.1 with one star. There is no second action to equip it on a hero: the bonus already takes part in the team's totals.

Star Advance consumes new fragments of that Treasure, following the quality's table. It does not raise the Rupture level or change the fragment's name. The costs checked for these tracks do not include extra gold or Stones; the resource charged is the fragment. The star shown on the row is the target star, including the first activation.

Example: an SSR Seed of the Gods needs forty fragments to activate and another forty to go from one to two stars. Starting from zero, reaching two stars requires eighty of its fragments. The maximum of six requires 640 in total. Do not multiply forty by six, because the later steps have higher prices.

secoes.titulo: Rupture: improving the level with specific stones

blocos.x: The Rupture tab improves the Treasure's level, paying three types of stone in the amount shown. A Treasure must be active before it receives a level. For SR and SSR, there are twelve payments, from Lv.1 to Lv.13. R has no such payments because its level skill has only the first entry.

Each row of the table charges three stones in the same amount. Solar Trio means Sunlight Stone, Moonlight Stone and Spinel Stone. Emerald Trio means Emerald Stone, Fire Spirit Stone and Lingbi Stone. If the amount twenty appears, it is twenty of each of the three, not twenty split among them. The +1, +2, +3, +4 or +5 mark also matters: Sunlight +1 does not replace Sunlight +2. The recipes on this track do not use a generic stone.

Note that SR and SSR do not start with the same trio. On the first Rupture of an SR it is two Sunlight+1, two Moonlight+1 and two Spinel+1. On SSR it is four Emerald+1, four Fire Spirit+1 and four Lingbi+1. The higher target level uses materials of higher marks; gather the exact trio shown for your object.

At Lv.13, the button hits the real cap. The empty entries after the last payment do not create a free Lv.14. Check the piece's level and materials before farming, because SR and SSR shift the cost sequence between the trios.

secoes.titulo: How stars and level change the bonuses

blocos.x: An active Treasure can combine percentage base attributes with a fixed attribute that grows with level. Stars raise the base percentages according to the object and multiply the part tied to the level. The first star uses the level value with no increase; the second adds twenty percent; the third thirty, and so on, up to one hundred percent on the tenth.

That is why raising a star can improve a piece already developed by Rupture without resetting its level. Conversely, raising the level increases the fixed part, keeping the current star's base percentages. The details show the current and next comparison; read the two axes separately to choose between spending fragments or stones.

Yamcha's Sword SR gives three hundred ATK and one percent HP at Lv.1/1★. At Lv.2/1★, the ATK goes to 350. At Lv.2/2★, the 350 receives twenty percent, resulting in 420 ATK, and the base HP bonus goes to 1.5%. At Lv.13/10★, the object gives 1,800 ATK and 5.5% HP.

Seed of the Gods SSR starts with 4,000 fixed HP, one percent DEF and four percent skill damage. At Lv.13/6★, the 16,000 HP from the level table receive sixty percent, resulting in 25,600 HP. DEF reaches 3.5% and skill damage nine percent. These are bonuses of the object; they are not each warrior's final sheet after all the formulas.

secoes.titulo: Sets: all members and the lowest star

blocos.x: A set only activates when all members are active. Its star is the lowest star among the members. If one of the pieces has five stars and the other only one, the set stays at the first grade. If a member is missing, the set is inactive, even if the others have many stars.

The objects' individual attributes keep adding up independently of the set. The set adds a passive for the team according to the current grade. It does not execute all the previous grades at once; the rule uses the version matching the lowest star. The set screen should be read together with the Total Bonus, which gathers the attributes of the activated objects.

Destroyer Fist is a checked example: its two SSR members give an extra damage passive against Attack-type enemies. With both activated at one star, the set gives five percent. The progression goes to six, seven, eight, nine and ten percent at grades two to six. If only one member reaches grade six, the second limits the result.

Summon > Treasure uses Combat Equipment Summon Scrolls. One pull costs one Scroll or two hundred Stones; ten cost ten Scrolls or two thousand Stones. When there are enough Scrolls for the whole button, they take priority. There is a free one daily when available, renewed at 5 AM, separate from paid purchases.

Each button has fifty paid purchases per day. So fifty x10 purchases represent five hundred pulls, in addition to the single purchases allowed by the other counter. Each pull includes a small Warrior EXP. The important result of this mode is fragments: the full R prize delivers twenty, SR thirty and SSR forty, enough to activate an object of that quality, but you still have to confirm the activation on the Treasure screen.

The table has an SSR guarantee at eighty pulls without the SSR group coming out. When it comes out earlier, the guarantee counter restarts. An x10 purchase makes ten pulls; it is not a single count for that guarantee. The guaranteed prize is the SSR group of forty fragments, not the specific SSR you prefer. The consulted preview of that group contains 29 SSR objects, while the full catalog has 45: do not promise to get every SSR in this tab.

The configuration also has a category of smaller fragments, in batches of five or ten. The weights eighty, fifteen, three and one of the selection add up to 99 and are affected by the guarantee. They should not be presented as eighty, fifteen, three and one percent. The guarantee limits streaks without SSR; it does not fix how many pulls it will take you to get a chosen piece.

secoes.titulo: Stone sources and planning without invented recipes

blocos.x: The sources of Rupture stones point to Elite stages, and the real prize of the stages checked confirms the examples. Elite 1-5 gives a Sunlight Stone+1; Elite 2-1 gives an Emerald Stone+1; Elite 9-5 gives a Sunlight Stone+5. Each attempt examined costs six Stamina and requires having opened the stage and its previous sequence. Read the specific material's source to choose the right stage.

Do not swap a stage's preview for a crafting recipe. The composition investigated does not define conversion of +1 stones into +2 or +4 into +5. For a Rupture that requires Sunlight+2, look for the source of that mark, instead of accumulating only Sunlight+1 expecting an automatic transformation.

Plan the set by its lowest-star member. If both need to reach the third grade, additional fragments of the member that is already at the fifth do not raise the grade while the other stays at the second. The stones, in turn, serve the piece's level and do not solve this set lock.

The current logic offers no dismantling, transfer to a hero or Treasure rebirth. There is no promise of a refund of fragments or of the stones paid in Rupture. Checking Details, Set and Total Bonus consumes no resource; spending occurs on confirming Star Advance or Rupture. Prioritize these previews before a final action.

guias.subtitulo: How to use and level up this system
guias.resumo: Master Training develops seven beasts that add bonuses to all warriors. Each attempt consumes Training Points and can raise or lower attributes; the result only takes effect after Save. The limits rise with the account level.

visao.x: Go to Support on the home screen and choose Master Training. The system opens for regular accounts at level 47; the card may appear earlier and stay locked until you meet the requirement.

The next sections explain how it works, how it levels up and where to get materials. The cost of an upgrade depends on the level and the item you choose. Check the preview of your action before confirming.

blocos.x: Open Support and enter Master Training. Access opens at account level 47. The first beast has an internal requirement of 1, but that value does not bring forward the system's normal opening in the hub. The others are unlocked at 54, 61, 68, 75, 82 and 95.

Each beast requires the previous one to be unlocked; you do not need to train it to the maximum to open the next. Unlocking charges no materials or currency. The cost appears when you ask for a training attempt.

The saved bonuses of all beasts are added up. They apply to all warriors, and the beast chosen on screen only indicates which one will be trained now. Choosing another does not deactivate the gain already saved on the others. All of them add ATK, DEF and HP; the two additional attributes vary by beast.

Choose an unlocked beast in the bottom strip. Check the five current attributes and their caps. Each bar shows how much has been developed relative to the account level's limit. The value on the left is the saved one; the limit is not a prize received when opening the beast.

Use Train x1 for one attempt or Train x10 for a batch of ten. The cost is debited when the training is requested, before the Save/Cancel choice. The comparison shows the proposed result and the difference of each attribute against what was saved.

Save replaces the five old values with the five new ones and closes the pending result. The choice saves the whole set, including any drops; there is no button to accept only the positive lines of the same result. While there is a pending result for that beast, the new-attempt buttons are replaced by Save and Cancel.

items: Check your Training Points balance and the cost of the action you intend to use.
Train once or ten times and read all five differences.
If you decide to keep the proposed set, tap Save.
If there is a loss and you prefer to keep the previous set, tap Cancel.
Resolve the result before starting another attempt on the same beast.

secoes.titulo: Cancel does not refund the cost

blocos.x: Cancel discards the proposal and keeps the previously saved attributes. The Training Points and currency already paid for the attempt are not refunded. So canceling a batch of ten does not make it a free training: you reject the result, but keep the expense.

In the native app consulted, Cancel turns gray when none of the five attributes dropped. Tapping in that situation only shows the game's notice; the result is not discarded. This also applies if all attributes stayed the same. For that pending result, use Save.

The web screen lets you confirm discarding a set with no drop. That behavior is not that of the current native button and should not be used as a mandatory step for those playing on the APK. The charging and Save rules still depend on the whole set.

The material actually used by the seven trainings is Training Points, item 201000. Although the beast catalog contains Dragon Ball names in themed texts, the attempts do not charge seven different materials. The amount varies: 5 on the first four, 10 on Super Shenron and Vados, 20 on the Grand Priest.

The data define three modes: Common pays only points; Advanced pays points plus 10,000 gold per attempt; Supreme pays points plus 10 Dragon Stones. The batch of ten multiplies all costs by ten, with no configured discount.

Divergence in the version consulted: the native screen shows the Advanced cost line, but its initial query returns the Common mode and uses it in the following actions. So the line displayed does not prove gold is charged. The table below documents the configured costs; it does not claim that the three modes can be selected on the APK's current screen.

Under the Common contract, ten trainings of the Earth Shenron cost 50 Training Points, with no gold. Under the Advanced contract, the same batch costs 50 points and 100,000 gold. Under the Supreme contract, it costs 50 points and 100 Stones. Under any of these contracts, canceling afterward does not refund the costs paid.

For Vados, ten configured Advanced attempts require 100 points and 100,000 gold; for the Grand Priest, they require 200 points and 100,000 gold. The increase in the amount of material does not raise the gold price per attempt: the extra remains 10,000.

The quantity ten does not mean ten guaranteed improvements. The batch adds up ten variations of each attribute and presents a single final set to Save or Cancel. One attribute can go up while another goes down; read the full comparison before accepting.

Each attribute's cap depends on the account's current level. Training limits the result between zero and that cap. When the account levels up, new limits may open room to keep developing an already trained beast. Leveling up the account does not by itself fill the bars automatically.

At level 100, the first six trainings have fixed caps of 1,500 ATK, 800 DEF and 7,500 HP. The Grand Priest has double those three limits. The maximum rates depend on each beast's attribute pair; compare with the unlock table to know which attribute each column belongs to.

The cap data reach level 135. Above the last tabulated level, the query keeps the last line available; this does not establish the account's maximum reachable level nor an infinite progression of the bonuses. No number in this guide was extrapolated beyond the existing lines.

The unlock levels remain mandatory. The cap lines for 50/80 also record numbers for beasts that cannot yet be trained at those levels; consulting them does not unlock those beasts. At level 100, all seven already meet the level requirement.

secoes.titulo: How to interpret gains and drops

blocos.x: Training can deliver negative variation. The name Supreme does not mean protection against drops or a guaranteed gain. The modes' parameters make their lower limit different, but all current ranges include negative values.

The recreation uses its own draw rule based on the parameters provided: for each attribute, each attempt calculates a variation proportional to the account level, to the beast's constant and to that attribute's factor. The result respects the zero-to-cap range. The random algorithm of the original commercial server is not available; there is no proven original success percentage to put in this guide.

The safe example is to compare values: if the saved ATK is 400 and the proposal is 430, accepting adds 30 ATK to that beast's contribution. If the same proposal lowers DEF from 200 to 195, Save also accepts that loss of 5. Canceling with that drop keeps 400/200, with no refund of the attempt's costs.

The sum of the saved bonuses goes into the warriors' attribute preparation. The CP notification requires a positive increase in the lineup's real CP; pending proposals, material spending and cancellation should not be read as a final gain.

secoes.titulo: Material sources and limits of interpretation

blocos.x: When Training Points run short, the app opens Source. That item's catalog points to Cultivation Path, stage 1; Supreme Warrior; and Nightmare Stage. The paths match the Training shortcuts in Image, tournament and Story. They provide neither a chance nor an amount of material per attempt in this survey.

The translated texts of some sources do not match the link's destination. Check the item in the mode's prizes or offer before spending resources to obtain it. The correct name of the material in the current data is Training Points; the guide does not call it a potion or a specific Dragon Ball.

On Vados, the second special bonus is defined as Supreme Defense, but the native bridge lacks the name of that key and may show ATK as a substitute label. The data attribute remains Supreme Defense. There are also incomplete themed descriptions on Vados and the Grand Priest; they were not used to invent additional skills.

This guide covers the attempts, their costs, the comparison, Save/Cancel and the limits present in the current rule. There is no star promotion or beast rupture in this flow. It also does not replace the grant of new warriors or the individual level trainings on the Warrior screen.

guias.subtitulo: How to use and level up this system

blocos.x: Open Support > Saiyan Soul, choose a book and then a word. Activate consumes the souls listed and enables that word's first quality. Upgrade consumes the cost of the next quality. The Preview shows the steps before you spend; the backpack opens the souls tab in the Bag.

The total Value adds up the current value of all active words, including those from earlier books. It unlocks the following books: you do not need to concentrate everything in the book you are viewing. The four current books are marked as open by the catalog, but their total Value requirements still apply to a regular account.

Soul Value, bonus points and attributes are different things. An upgrade can raise HP and Value without giving any elemental point. The current attribute replaces that of the previous step; the values of all stars of the same word are not added. Distinct words, on the other hand, accumulate their attributes for the account.

secoes.titulo: Two real recipes and how to compare the investment

blocos.x: Battle Maniac, from the first book, uses Goku - Saiyan Soul. Activation consumes one unit and gives 30 HP, Value 1 and zero points. Each of the four upgrades also asks for one unit. So five complete souls take that word to its last step: 90 HP and Value 5, still with no points. Do not expect 300 HP from adding the five values in the preview.

Saiyan, from the Z Warrior book, asks for Kale - Saiyan Soul. Activation gives 72 ATK, Value 2 and one point; the next upgrade gives 144 ATK, Value 4 and two points. The second step consumes one more Kale soul and adds one net point: it does not add the two points again to those already earned.

The same souls can take part in several words. Spending a copy on one recipe reduces the balance available for the others. Compare the next attribute, the Value needed for the new book and the points missing in the preset before using a choice box. Open Bonus to distribute the points across eight lines: damage against Wind / Fire / Earth / Water and resistance against Wind / Fire / Earth / Water. The percentage is directed at the indicated opposing element, not an unrestricted ATK bonus or a universal damage reduction.

Each level adds one percentage point to the line's final value, up to level 50, or 50%. The cost is bonus points, not Gold or Stones. Increasing with + requires free points; decreasing with - returns availability when the accumulated cost is recalculated. There is no currency charge for this redistribution.

There are four presets, each with its own independent distribution within the same total of points earned. They do not quadruple your reserve. Only the one marked Current enters the fight; editing another does not automatically swap the active one. Use the Use button to switch plans and rename the tabs to identify the opponent or the type of resistance you want.

The first ten levels cost ten points in total and give 10% on that line. Taking a line from 0 to 50 costs 195 points. With one point, for example, you can use 1% damage against Fire in one preset and 1% resistance against Water in another, but not apply both at the same time if only one distribution is active.

blocos.x: Summon > Saiyan Soul offers 1x for 400 Stones and 5x for 2,000 Stones. The Saiyan Soul Summon Coupon replaces the currency when you have one or five coupons, respectively. Neither button has a daily free pull in the current catalog. The limits are separate: 50 paid purchases per button, renewed at 05:00; the 5x pack offers no discount.

When a word lacks material, the quick acquisition first checks the selectable Common, Epic and Legendary boxes in the Bag. It only proposes consuming boxes that can cover the souls needed. Confirming the conversion delivers the souls; go back to activate or upgrade the word afterward. Check which soul each box lets you choose: a Common box does not choose Kale, for example, while the Legendary includes that soul.

The Soul Shop is reachable through the Shop button and has four tabs at level 56. It charges Saiyan Spirit, also called Saiyan Soul Essence in the texts. Fixed examples from the catalog: a Goku Soul costs 80; one of Hit, Goku SSG, Broly or Beerus costs 1250. Offers have their own stock and revalidation; confirm the price and quantity shown before buying.

In the current native flow, the quick-acquisition shortcut converts boxes or opens Sources; it does not run the automatic purchase of souls in the shop. Use the Shop button for that manual purchase. The web client also has that automatic path, so the two interfaces should not be described as identical on this point.

The Summon contains souls and additional rewards, but does not guarantee the specific soul needed on each attempt. Limited Offers and the Saiyan Soul Pass are conditional on the activity in effect. This research did not confirm a continuous source of Saiyan Spirit; do not present it as an easy currency or one renewed for free every day.

Resonance is the individual part: its skill only applies to the warrior bound to the weapon. A weapon has one bearer and a warrior can keep only one research weapon. Selecting another bearer or removing the bond changes who receives the resonance, without removing the general attributes of the marks from the account.

Go to Support > Weapons, select the weapon, check its marks, the attribute panel and the effect description. Activate corresponds to the first star. Once resonance is available, use Equip and choose an owned warrior; None removes the bond. Equipping does not charge fragments or Gold.

secoes.titulo: Marks: correct material, value and cap

blocos.x: Tap a mark and choose Upgrade. Each upgrade spends the material matching that mark's quality and attribute; there is no Gold charge to raise the mark. The current qualities are Elite, Epic and Legendary, with materials I for ATK, II for DEF and III for HP.

Each mark starts at level 0 and can reach 80. The consumption curve is the same across the three qualities: level 1 to 5 costs one unit per step; 6 to 10 costs two; and so on, rising by one unit per block of five, up to 16 per step from 76 to 80. The total from 0 to 80 is 680 units of that mark's specific material.

The mark's value is its level's attribute multiplied by the weapon's star factor, rounded down. With no star, the factor is 1. At the first star it becomes 1.03; at the second 1.06; at the tenth 1.30. Upgrading one weapon does not multiply the marks of the others.

Example: an Elite Attack Mark on the Lava Sword at level 5 is worth 50 ATK before stars. With the weapon at the second star, it is worth 53 ATK. At the first star it is still worth 51 ATK. The mark's level, and not the bearer warrior's level, determines this base.

secoes.titulo: Activating, raising stars and preparing the six marks

blocos.x: Activating the first star of any of the six weapons asks for 40 fragments of the weapon itself and 200,000 Gold. In that first step there is no minimum mark level. The second star also requires no minimum level; from the third on, all six marks must reach the table's tier. Upgrading only the strongest does not solve the requirement: what sets the block is the lowest-level mark.

The cap is ten stars. The base rate grows from 6% at the first to 24% at the tenth, while the marks' multiplication grows from 3% to 30%. The full path from 0 to 10 stars costs 1,200 own fragments and 6,600,000 Gold; this does not include the marks' consumption.

Resonance has versions at stars 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10. Only the highest version reached is applied; six copies of the skill do not stack. Stars 3, 5, 7 and 9 keep strengthening the base rate and the marks even without swapping the resonance version.

As a tactical example, the Angel's Scepter's initial description heals the team from the second round and has a limit of one action per battle. At the fourth star the described limit rises to two. At the tenth, the description goes to 125% of ATK on the main heal, an extra 40% for targets below 40% HP and one charge of Damage Immunity for everyone, up to three times. These texts serve to compare versions; the benefit depends on binding the weapon to the warrior.
All stars: costs and conditions
Tiers are levels of that weapon's six marks, not the account level. +30% means multiplying the base by 1.30.

The Summon button opens the Weapons tab, which may appear with the label Battle Equip. Buying 1x costs 200 Dragon Stones or one Summon Cube; 10x costs 2,000 Stones or ten Cubes. There is no free pull in the current catalog, and the 10x pack has no discount. The limit is 50 paid purchases on each button per day, with a reset at 05:00.

The reward tables contain fragments of the six weapons and mark materials in the three qualities. The draw can give different amounts. The ScienceBox_10 guarantee kicks in after 100 pulls without its reset reward coming out; that reward is 40 fragments of a random weapon among the six. A drop from that category before the limit restarts the count. It is not an additional weapon every 100 pulls nor does it let you choose the model.

Limited Offers and the Weapon Summon's times chest are event shortcuts, subject to the account's term and conditions. The Sources list may say Coming soon... even though the destination is the Weapons tab already implemented; prefer the screen actually accessible and its current content. The guide does not assign acquisition percentages from partial table weights.

To advance with few materials, first see which of the six marks blocks the next star and concentrate the needed type on it. Choose the bearer by the resonance's trigger: a weapon that depends on Supreme favors whoever can use it; the Ring and the Scepter have different HP / round conditions. There is no proven best universal weapon in this catalog.

guias.titulo: Divine Realm: Artifacts, pieces and stars
guias.subtitulo: How to use and level up this system
guias.resumo: The Divine Realm gathers Artifacts that raise the attributes of the whole team and add support skills. The system appears at Lv.75 and opens at account Lv.78. Unlocking an Artifact, completing its pieces and upgrading its star are separate investments. The five Artifacts of Divine Realm I can evolve up to five stars and twelve stages.

visao.x: Go to Support on the home screen and choose Divine Realm: Artifacts, pieces and stars. The system opens for regular accounts at level 78; the card may appear earlier and stay locked until you meet the requirement.

The next sections explain how it works, how it levels up and where to get materials. The cost of an upgrade depends on the level and the item you choose. Check the preview of your action before confirming.

secoes.titulo: What you unlock and who receives the bonus

blocos.x: Go to Support > Artifact to see the list. The five Artifacts are North Kai, East Supreme Kai, Heles, Fused Zamasu and Grand Kai. Each has its own fragment: Kai fragments do not activate Heles. You can develop several at once; the bonus does not depend on equipping a single Artifact on a warrior.

Installed pieces provide fixed ATK, DEF and HP to all warriors on the team. Activated Artifacts also send a skill according to the current star. The attributes of all developed Artifacts add up. So having two active Artifacts does not turn off the first and does not require moving a piece between heroes.

The individual activation data indicate Lv.75, but the system's normal opening is Lv.78. For a regular account, the menu access is the requirement that lets you reach the screen. Do not treat an Artifact's individual field as authorization to enter before the system's opening level.

To unlock an Artifact, gather sixty of its fragments and confirm the activation. The activation checked charges no additional gold. The new Artifact comes with one star, stage one and six piece slots still empty. The star does not mean the six pieces were already bought: attribute evolution starts when you install the pieces.

After activation, tap each piece in the Strengthen tab. It is acquired with Divine Essence and installed immediately. In the first stage, each costs ten Essence; completing all six costs sixty. The pieces have distinct attributes: two give ATK, two HP and two DEF. You can install part of them and continue later; the bonus of the pieces already installed starts to count.

Equip All goes through the six slots and installs only the pieces it can pay for. If the balance runs out, the Artifact may be left incomplete. Do not read the button as a guaranteed purchase of the whole set nor as a free action. Before pressing Advance, check the six slots and the balance.

items: Fragments are for activation and stars.
Divine Essence is for the stage pieces.

secoes.titulo: The twelve stages and the accumulated gain

blocos.x: Advance requires the six pieces of the current stage to be installed. Confirming opens the next stage and shows six new slots; the attributes of the completed steps stay accumulated. There is no extra charge on the Advance button: the charge already happened when installing the pieces. Step twelve is the cap, but you can still complete its six pieces to get the whole bonus.

The table records the cost per piece, the cost to complete that step and the attribute increase of the six pieces. The values in the last column are increments of the stage, not the Artifact's accumulated total. Adding up the twelve steps lets you plan the maximum investment without confusing a current→next preview with the full gain.

Example: completing stages one and two costs 180 Divine Essence and grants 220 ATK, 110 DEF and 1,760 HP to the team. If, at stage three, you install only one of the ATK pieces, you will add only that piece's attribute; you will not yet have the whole increment of the third row.

Completing the seventy-two pieces of an Artifact, spread across the twelve stages, requires 10,320 Divine Essence. The fixed result is 3,360 ATK, 1,680 DEF and 26,880 HP for the team. These attributes do not include the star skill, the warriors' attributes or the multipliers of other systems.

The five Artifacts I use the same piece progression. If all are fully completed, the sum of the pieces is 16,800 ATK, 8,400 DEF and 134,400 HP. That requires 51,600 Divine Essence, besides the activation fragments. The sum serves as a reference for the system's ceiling; it is not a Combat Power value that will appear on its own on the sheet.

As the cost per piece grows with the stage, you can compare the next increment with that of another Artifact still at a low step. There is no single priority formula: the star also changes skills with different conditions. Compare the fixed gain your Essence buys and the skill your team needs before concentrating all the fragments on a single track.

secoes.titulo: Upgrading the star and reading the right skill

blocos.x: The Star tab uses the Artifact's own fragments and gold. Activation already puts on the first star; the costs below lead to the second, third, fourth and fifth. The fragments paid are consumed, with no requirement to complete all the stages before the star upgrade. The fifth is the cap of this track.

From activated with one star up to five stars, you spend 420 fragments and eight million gold. Including the sixty for activation, the total from locked is 480 fragments of the Artifact itself. These values are per Artifact, and the Divine Essence of the pieces is an additional, independent investment.

The skill used is that of the current star: five versions of the same skill do not stack. Open the stars information to compare the current and next effect. Some skills have a maximum number of activations per battle, turn conditions, targets and chance; raising a star can change more than one of these factors.

secoes.titulo: Examples of skills and reading conditions

blocos.x: Grand Kai offers a simple example of cumulative evolution within the skill's description: the first star gives six percent damage reduction; the following ones add crit resistance, crit rate, damage and crit damage. At the fifth, the current version includes the benefits described earlier. This is different from running five separate skills.

North Kai has healing tied to receiving Supreme damage in the first three rounds. The first star asks for five occurrences and heals the two lowest-HP allies by six percent, with one activation; the fifth changes to four occurrences, four allies, twelve percent and up to two activations. The bonus is not equivalent to automatic healing every round.

East Supreme Kai, Heles and Fused Zamasu have Rage rules, conditional attacks and additional attacks. Read on the screen itself the star you are aiming for, including the usage limits. The catalog's literal conditions were checked; this guide does not replace the individual description with a promise that every attack or every ally triggers the effect.

secoes.titulo: Summoning and getting the right materials

blocos.x: The Summon > Artifact I tab uses the Divine Realm Summon Ticket. One pull costs one ticket or eighty Stones; ten cost ten tickets or eight hundred Stones. Enough tickets are used before Stones. There is a free daily option when available, renewed at 5 AM; do not count a free purchase as a paid purchase toward the limit.

The limit is fifty paid purchases per button, with separate x1 and x10 counters. Each pull also gives a small Warrior EXP. The summon can deliver Divine Essence or fragments of the five Artifacts. The tables checked include batches of five, ten, twenty-five or thirty Essence, and of one, two, three or five fragments of an Artifact.

The numbers one, four and five in the preview belong to chained cycles of the draw. They do not establish an independent percentage for getting exactly Heles or exactly thirty Essence. There is no guarantee of a complete activation in ten pulls. The times chest and the event shop, when active and visible, should be checked in the real edition; pieces are not granted just by opening the menu.

The Essence and fragments source shortcut points to Artifact Summon, although some legacy texts mention Judgment of the Five Warriors or another Artifact name. The acquisition confirmed here is the summon and its tables. No reward from another mode is added just because a shortcut text mentions it.

There is inspection data for study, but the configurations for Artifacts six to ten and part of the art are missing. It is not a playable extension promised for your progress at Lv.78.

The menu appears at account Lv.78 and opens at Lv.80. This system is separate from the Emblems and Tomes of normal equipment.

secoes.titulo: Four slots per warrior and one rule for the account

blocos.x: Each warrior has four slots. The first becomes available at the warrior's third star; the following ones require six, eight and ten stars. Tap the unlocked slot to open it and choose an Emblem. Opening a slot, as checked, charges no additional item. The star required is the warrior's, not that of the Emblem you intend to equip.

Emblems have their own group, type, star and level. A group represents the same Emblem family across its different stars. Only one Emblem of each group can be equipped across the whole account: equipping another Karin-sama on a second warrior removes the Karin-sama that was on the first. You are not allowed to get around this rule by using two different qualities or stars of the same family.

The four slots can receive different groups. Some pieces have a restriction on warrior or hero type; check the piece's indication when selecting. Equip All uses open empty slots and compatible free pieces, respecting the groups already used. Remove All frees the pieces, without destroying or refunding the investment.

secoes.titulo: Level, star and attributes are different things

blocos.x: A received Emblem starts at Lv.0. Upgrading uses Emblem Essence and raises its level up to Lv.20. The level strengthens attributes and is also passed on to the piece's skill. The star belongs to the Emblem's model; raising the level does not automatically raise its star nor unlock a new piece family.

The attributes are calculated from the piece's base value and a growth per level. Lv.1 matches the base value; Lv.0 sits one growth below it. Do not add the base value to the growth twenty times to calculate Lv.20: from Lv.1 on there are nineteen increments.

For example, a two-star Ox-King at Lv.0 gives 270 ATK, 108 DEF and 2,160 HP. At Lv.1, it gives 302 ATK, 121 DEF and 2,412 HP. At Lv.20, it gives 910 ATK, 368 DEF and 7,200 HP. These are the piece's attributes on the bearer, before the sheet's other bonuses. The skill and the attributes of the chosen group need to be compared together; the number of stars alone does not identify usefulness for your team.

secoes.titulo: How much it costs to upgrade

blocos.x: The Essence required depends on the Emblem and the star. Each tap charges the next level, using that model's row. There is no single price that serves all pieces. The table shows representative examples, including the accumulated cost from Lv.0 to Lv.5 and to Lv.20.

A two-star Ox-King pays one hundred Essence for Lv.1, two hundred for Lv.2 and so on, up to two thousand for the last level. The total up to Lv.20 is 21,000. A four-star Karin-sama starts with one hundred, then two hundred and four hundred; it ends at 3,800. The total is 38,100, although the first tap costs the same as the Ox-King's.

Do not use the availability of Essence as a reason to consume a piece that serves as star material. First choose which groups will stay equipped and which will be ingredients. A piece that will be consumed in Fusion does not automatically return its levels' Essence: restore it first if the goal is to preserve part of that material.

secoes.titulo: Raising the piece's star or crafting through Fusion

blocos.x: There are two related paths, but their availability depends on the client. On the web client, Star Up improves an existing Emblem that has an evolution configured. The Emblem itself is preserved with its current level, limited to the new model's cap. Materials of the same family and those of any family must have the required star; the copy you are upgrading already counts as part of the copies needed. In the native APK examined, the operation exposed is the Fusion that crafts the target at Lv.0; there is no corresponding Star Up call that preserves the level.

Example: upgrading Karin-sama from four to five stars uses your Karin-sama, plus one four-star Karin-sama, plus any four-star Emblem and three hundred Emblem Crystals. The level of the Karin-sama you chose to upgrade is preserved. The other two ingredients disappear. If they were upgraded, do not count on an automatic refund of that Essence.

Fusion chooses a target Emblem and fills each position of the recipe. Copy means the same family, one star below the target. Any means an Emblem of any family, also one star below. All ingredients must be free, distinct and not used in another position of the recipe. Fusion creates a new piece at Lv.0 and consumes the old ones; it does not choose which ingredient level to preserve.

Not every family has every advancement. Karin-sama ends at five stars on the track examined, while Arale has models of six, seven and eight. Stop at the cap shown for that piece. Do not turn the screen's visual constant of seven stars into a claim that there are no eight-star models in the catalog.

secoes.titulo: Choosing materials without losing a useful piece

blocos.x: Before confirming a Fusion, check the number of copy and any positions. Recipes are not all the same: Arale 7 requires one copy and one free ingredient of any family; the eight-star one requires two copies and one more of any family. The cost in Cores also changes. Follow the recipe shown for the target, without mentally reusing the previous star's recipe.

An equipped ingredient is unavailable. Removing it from the warrior does not change its star or level, but makes the piece free for selection. Choosing materials is a preview; the charge and the destruction happen when you confirm the composition. Before that confirmation, review whether you selected a group you meant to reserve for another warrior.

The native operation also prevents crafting a seven-star target again when exactly that model already exists on the account. Having a grayed-out Emblem in the bag may indicate that its family is already equipped elsewhere, not that the item disappeared. Check the owner and the rule of one equipped group per account before trying to duplicate the same bonus.

Restoration returns part of the Essence spent on levels and takes the Emblem back to Lv.0, keeping its family and star. The common option returns eighty percent, rounded up, and charges no Stones. The advanced one returns one hundred percent and costs two percent of the Essence returned in Stones, also rounded up.

A two-star Ox-King at Lv.5 spent 1,500 Essence. Common Restoration returns 1,200 and keeps the piece at Lv.0; the advanced one returns the 1,500 for thirty Stones. At Lv.20, the same model spent 21,000: common returns 16,800; advanced returns 21,000 for 420 Stones.

That refund only covers the level upgrade. Crystals, Cores and Emblems that were consumed to craft or upgrade a star are not returned. Restoration does not lower the star, does not recreate ingredients and does not split a strong Emblem into its former copies. Compare the cost in Stones with the amount of Essence before choosing the advanced option.

secoes.titulo: Dismantling and getting Essence or Crystals

blocos.x: Dismantle destroys a free Emblem and delivers the star's fixed prize, plus all the Essence spent on its levels. This action differs from Restoration: the piece ceases to exist. The native dismantle list excludes equipped pieces and pieces of seven stars or more. The quick selection lets you tick star ranges, but the confirmation should be reviewed piece by piece.

A four-star Karin-sama at Lv.0 delivers two hundred Essence and thirty Crystals. If it is at Lv.5, with 2,100 Essence invested, it delivers 2,300 Essence in all and the same thirty Crystals. The star defines the fixed prize; the levels add only the refund of the Essence invested. There is no refund of the copies that built that piece.

Emblem Crystal and Emblem Essence are different materials: the first goes into Fusions and the second into levels. Soul Emblem Core is a separate item used in high recipes. Summoning and decomposition are proven sources of the pieces and materials below; a fixed source of Cores was not established by the data consulted.

In Summon > Emblem, the single purchase costs one Soul Insignia Summon Ticket or 150 Stones. This tab's batch is x5: it costs five tickets or 750 Stones. It is not a purchase of ten, even if the screen's internal component shares the position used by x10 in other tabs. Enough tickets take priority over Stones.

There is no free pull configured in this tab. Each button has fifty paid purchases per day, renewed at 5 AM; fifty x5 purchases represent 250 pulls. Each pull adds a small Warrior EXP as an extra. The Soul Seal preview shows which families and stars take part, including models of two to five stars.

The draw tables use chained cycles. The preview's weights two, two and one are not an independent rate of getting a five-star piece. The main cycle of the batch of five also goes through a sublist that alternates prizes: this guide does not promise a five-star per x5 purchase. Use the preview to check the possible catalog, without converting its weights into percentages for a specific piece.
